agent_domain.description: Whether this deployment fronts the AGENT domain (PRD decision 40.7: meetings, agents and flows work independently and in any configuration, identity being the only shared dependency). Presence is a configuration fact — whether the deployment named the door — never a probe: a probe makes "agent-api is restarting" and "there is no agent-api" the same answer, and the second is a shipped product.
agent_domain.when_unconfigured: The edge registers no /agent/* route and assembles no agent rows into its scope table, so a request to /agent/anything is 404 — this deployment does not serve it — rather than a 401 about a route that is not here. Everything else is unchanged: this is the `no-agents` product of decision 40.6 (gateway + meetings + flows + identity), not a degraded gateway.

keys.description: shared internal secret attached as X-Internal-Secret on the admin-api /internal/validate hop (adapters.py:67-69). Unset, admin-api rejects validation and EVERY API-key check 503s (fail-closed) — so the boot refuses instead of coming up green and 503ing every call (the 2026-04-23 failure shape, #526). It is ALSO the internal-tier authority agent-api's _internal_caller and admin-api's _check_internal compare against, which is why a published placeholder is refused outright (F95).

§1.10, §6.9 F-E: the key ring the gateway signs x-user-id with, in the webhook secret encryption ring's format: JSON {"<kid>": "<exactly 32 bytes, base64>"}, a kid being 1-64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - (identity_signature.py). Every request forwarded with x-user-id carries x-gateway-signature: kid=<kid>,t=<unix>,v2=<hex HMAC-SHA256> over the kid, t, x-user-id and every other identity header the gateway forwards (email, scopes, limits, workspaces, webhook url, secret and events), method, body SHA-256, raw query and path (core/gateway/contracts/gateway-identity). meeting-api and admin-api hold the same ring. Unset, the boot refuses; set but malformed (bad JSON, a key that isn't 32 bytes, a bad kid), the boot refuses too, naming the fault and never a key; a gateway built without preflight refuses to forward (503).

§1.10, §6.9 F-E: the kid in GATEWAY_IDENTITY_KEYS the gateway signs with, named in every signature. It must be in the ring, or the boot refuses. Rotation: add the new key to the ring on all three services and roll; switch this to its kid and roll the gateway; later drop the old key from every ring and roll.

agent control-plane base URL fronted under /api/*. UNSET MEANS THE AGENT DOMAIN IS NOT DEPLOYED (PRD 40.6 no-agents, 40.7 domains are independent): the edge registers no /agent/* route and assembles no agent rows into its scope table, so a request there is 404 — this deployment does not serve it — rather than a 401 about a route that is not here. A URL default would assert the domain exists and make its absence unsayable.

pub/sub bus backing the /ws fan-in

§1.13: entry writes (PUT /v2/entries + POST /v2/entries/remove) allowed per account in each 60 s window, counted in Redis (REDIS_URL) and shared by every gateway replica (intake_limit.py). The write past it is 429 rate_limited with Retry-After = the seconds left in the window; with Redis unreachable those writes are 503 unavailable, never let through uncounted.

WS-6: the per-user token bucket's burst capacity (ratelimit.py) — every REST request forwarded at the single funnel (app._forward, keyed by the resolved user_id) costs one token; a request past an empty bucket is 429.
WS-6: the per-user token bucket's refill rate (tokens/s, ratelimit.py) — how fast a user's burst capacity comes back after being spent.
WS-6: a truthy value turns the per-user token bucket off (ratelimit.from_env); unset keeps it on. A debugging switch, not set by the chart.
